summary: Build on the current static frontend baseline rather than restarting it. The app already supports Excel paste input, optional headers, ranked candidate generation, and candidate selection. This round should preserve that logic, keep score calculations internal, replace the score-heavy result UI with compact tier-colored previews, and add a selected-candidate swap editor with immediate two-click updates. The older browser/mobile QA gap remains documented but is not a blocker for this iteration.

milestones.title: Editable Result Model
milestones.objective: Refactor the current candidate/result data so the UI can render compact previews and perform role-slot-based swaps without breaking the existing optimizer.
deliverables: Keep `src/lib/optimizer.js` ranking behavior and candidate generation rules unchanged in priority order: total score difference, role-score-difference sum, tank score difference, then unranked difference.
Extend the candidate/result shape so each visible slot has a stable slot id, fixed slot role, and linked player identity; do not rely on pre-rendered score text for UI state.

Add a small pure helper module such as `src/lib/editor.js` or equivalent for: creating an editable copy from a candidate, selecting a slot, swapping two slots, and rebuilding display assignments from the destination slot role.
Preserve internal metric fields on candidates/results so tests can still verify ranking logic even though the main UI stops showing score numbers.
Keep parser behavior intact, including header-present and headerless input support, duplicate-name validation, and Korean error messages.

milestones.title: Compact Preview UI
milestones.objective: Turn the current metric-heavy candidate area into a fast visual comparison surface that shows both teams and role placement at a glance.
deliverables: Update `src/lib/render.js`, `src/constants/copy.js`, and `src/styles.css` so the candidate list renders 6 compact preview cards, each with `팀 A` and `팀 B` mini layouts showing `1탱 2딜 2힐` slot placement.

Show each player with tier-driven visual styling using the required color mapping: unranked white, bronze bronze, silver silver, gold yellow, platinum mint, diamond blue, master green, grandmaster violet.
Move tier presentation to names/chips/backgrounds instead of numeric score text; remove visible personal score, team total score, and numeric score-difference display from the main UI.
Keep candidate ordering implicit through card order and default recommendation styling; the first ranked candidate must still appear as the default selected option.
Retain the existing input preview section but remove score numbers there as well, so the main UI consistently treats scores as hidden internal data.

milestones.title: Final Swap Editor
milestones.objective: Load the selected candidate into a single editable board and allow direct two-click swapping between slots with immediate rerender.
deliverables: Add editor state in `src/main.js` and `src/lib/appFlow.js` for at least `selectedCandidateId`, editable team data, and `selectedSwapSlotId`.
When the user clicks a candidate preview, load a fresh editable copy of that candidate into the final edit area and clear any previous pending slot selection.
Render the final edit area as one selected candidate only, with larger clickable slot cards/buttons for both teams; each slot must clearly show role and tier-colored player identity.
Implement the interaction rule exactly: first slot click marks selected state, second slot click swaps the two players, and the DOM updates immediately without rerunning clipboard parsing.

Make swaps slot-based, not role-based ownership-based: if a player moves into a new slot, that slot’s role applies and the displayed tier metadata must be recalculated from that player’s tier for the new role.
Allow swaps across teams and across different roles while preserving the fixed team slot structure of `1탱 2딜 2힐` per team.
Show short Korean helper text for the current interaction state, for example neutral guidance, first-slot-selected guidance, and post-swap completion guidance.

milestones.title: Verification And Handoff
milestones.objective: Lock the new behavior with deterministic tests and leave clear documentation for the next agent or reviewer.
deliverables: Extend `test/optimizer.test.js` so ranking assertions still prove the required sort order after the UI refactor.
Add focused unit tests for the new editor helper logic, especially cross-role swaps where displayed tier data must change with the destination slot.

Expand `test/appFlow.test.js` to cover: 6 compact candidates render, first candidate auto-loads into the final editor, candidate switching resets the editor to the newly selected candidate, first slot selection is highlighted, and second click swaps players immediately.
Add or update CSS-focused tests so the required tier color classes/tokens exist and the compact preview/editor layouts remain stacked and overflow-safe on narrow widths.
Run `npm test` and `npm run build` as mandatory verification. Keep `npm run test:browser` optional evidence only when a Chromium-family browser is available, and document clearly if it was skipped.
Update `README.md` and `FINAL_OUTPUT.md` to describe the compact preview workflow, swap editing behavior, score-hidden UI rule, and the non-blocking status of the older real-browser/mobile QA gap.

acceptance_criteria: Given the same valid 10-player input, the app shows exactly 6 distinct candidate combinations.
Each candidate preview is compact and shows both `팀 A` and `팀 B` with 5 visible role slots each.
Every candidate still satisfies `1탱 2딜 2힐` per team and does not duplicate any player within that candidate.
Candidate ordering still follows the required internal ranking priority: total score difference, role-score-difference sum, tank score difference, then unranked difference.
The first ranked candidate is selected by default and loaded into the final edit area immediately after calculation.
Candidate previews visually distinguish tiers with the required color mapping for all 8 tiers.
The main app UI does not show personal score values, team total scores, or numeric score-difference values by default.
Clicking a different candidate updates only the final edit area and does not clear the pasted input.
On the first slot click in the final edit area, that slot shows a selected state.
On the second slot click, the two selected slots swap players immediately and the updated names/tier styling are visible without page reload.
Cross-role swaps use the destination slot’s role when displaying the moved player’s tier information.
Selecting another candidate after making swaps replaces the editor with a fresh copy of that candidate and clears the previous swap selection.
Header-present input and headerless input both continue to parse correctly.
`npm test` and `npm run build` pass on the final workspace state.
test_strategy: Keep the existing parser tests for optional-header handling and validation errors; they should continue passing unchanged or with only copy updates.
Add pure unit tests for the new editable-candidate helper: initial slot mapping, first-slot selection state, same-team swap, cross-team swap, and cross-role swap with recomputed tier metadata.
Keep optimizer tests focused on ranking correctness and candidate uniqueness so UI refactoring cannot silently change balancing behavior.
Expand the fake-DOM app-flow test to assert that score text is absent from the rendered result UI while candidate cards, editor cards, and swap interactions still work.
Add CSS or render-contract tests for the eight tier color classes/tokens and for mobile-safe grid stacking of compact previews and the final editor.
Run `npm test` and `npm run build` before handoff; run `npm run test:browser` only if a supported browser exists, and record whether it ran or was skipped.

risks.risk: A swap implementation that only exchanges rendered assignment objects will show the wrong tier after cross-role swaps.
risks.mitigation: Store player identity separately from slot role and rebuild displayed assignment data from the destination slot role every time a swap occurs.

risks.risk: Removing visible score numbers can accidentally break the current candidate UI and tests because the existing render layer is score-centric.
risks.mitigation: Keep all scoring metrics in the candidate/result model, refactor tests to validate ranking in logic tests, and rewrite UI tests around structure, selection, and swap behavior instead of visible scores.

risks.risk: Compact preview cards can become too dense and overflow on narrow screens once both teams and 10 slots are shown.
risks.mitigation: Use a strict mini-slot layout with CSS grid, wrap-safe text, and responsive stacking, then lock it with existing style tests plus new compact-preview checks.

risks.risk: Manual edits can become confusing if users switch candidates and the app mixes old edited state with a newly selected candidate.
risks.mitigation: Define one clear rule: candidate selection always loads a fresh editable copy and clears pending swap state, then cover that rule in DOM tests and README copy.

risks.risk: The required white unranked color can lose contrast against the existing light UI theme.
risks.mitigation: Use white as the primary fill but add explicit border, shadow, and readable text colors so the chip/card remains distinguishable.

risks.risk: The repository still contains older round documentation and UI language that explicitly shows scores, which can mislead a junior builder.
risks.mitigation: Treat the user-provided iteration-3 spec as the active scope for this pass and update README/FINAL_OUTPUT so the shipped behavior and docs match the new score-hidden requirement.

risks.risk: Older real-browser/mobile QA findings may distract implementation even though this iteration marks them non-blocking.
risks.mitigation: Do not spend this round reopening browser-only work beyond keeping automated checks green; document the remaining QA gap honestly instead of treating it as feature scope.

definition_of_done: The existing paste, validation, candidate-generation, and default-recommendation flow still works.
The app renders 6 compact candidate previews that are easy to compare visually without exposing numeric scores.
The selected candidate loads into one final edit area where players can be swapped by two slot clicks.
Swaps update the UI immediately and correctly recalculate displayed tier information based on the destination slot role.
All tier colors follow the specified mapping in the main UI.
Header-present and headerless Excel-style paste input both still work.
Automated tests cover ranking, compact preview rendering, tier styling contracts, candidate selection, and swap behavior.
`README.md` and `FINAL_OUTPUT.md` reflect the new compact preview and swap-edit workflow and accurately describe verification scope for this round.
open_questions: Assumption: the user-provided iteration-3 spec supersedes the older score-visible requirements still present in the current workspace history.
Assumption: selecting a candidate loads a fresh editable copy of that candidate and discards unsaved swaps from any previously selected candidate.
Assumption: swaps are allowed between any two visible slots, including cross-team and cross-role swaps.
Assumption: the "do not show numeric scores" rule applies to the main app UI surfaces only; internal calculations and automated tests may still use numeric score fields.
Assumption: the tier-color requirement can be satisfied with tier-colored chips/cards plus readable text labels, not necessarily by coloring the entire team column.

Assumption: unresolved real-browser/mobile validation from earlier rounds remains documented but is intentionally non-blocking for this iteration unless a browser is available for optional smoke testing.
